status: drafted via multi-agent workflow, adversarially fact-checked and corrected
notes: 1 Timothy is a personal pastoral letter, not a narrative book, so most of its content indexes as law/theme tiers (11 of 13) rather than person tiers — Paul is instructing, not narrating events. Only Paul (the author, who personally recounts his own conversion/testimony in 1:12-16 and personally delivers Hymenaeus and Alexander to Satan) and Timothy (the letter's real, individually-addressed recipient, given personal charges about his youth, his ordination by prophecy and laying on of hands, and even his health — 5:23) meet the "personally embodied" bar for a full person-tier; the rest of the book's content — fables/genealogies, prayer for rulers, women's church conduct, bishop and deacon qualifications, the Mystery of Godliness creed, latter-day apostasy, widows, elders, servants, and the love of money — is pure instructional/doctrinal transmission from Paul, so it is indexed as law-type tiers with Paul as deliveredBy rather than forced into invented person-tiers. No separate Jesus tier was created for this book (unlike the Gospels) since Christ is referenced only doctrinally (the one Mediator, 2:5; manifest in the flesh, 3:16; witnessed before Pilate, 6:13) and never appears as a personally-acting character within the letter itself. Naming-collision flag: Hymenaeus (1:20) is paired with Alexander here, but a Hymenaeus also reappears (paired with Philetus) in 2 Timothy 2:17, and an Alexander the coppersmith appears separately in 2 Timothy 4:14 — the text never explicitly identifies these as the same men across the two letters, so no identity is asserted, only flagged. Pontius Pilate is mentioned once (6:13) purely as a historical reference point for Christ's own testimony, not as an active character in this book, so he is logged in genealogyLists rather than given a character entry. Correction pass: closed four verse-coverage gaps (1:17 doxology folded into Paul's testimony citation; 4:7-10's charge to refuse fables and pursue godliness folded into the Doctrines of Devils tier as its natural positive counterpart; 5:7 folded into the Widow Indeed tier between vv.6 and 8; 6:15-16's doxology folded into Timothy's charge citation, extending 6:11-14 to 6:11-16) and resolved an overlapping/imprecise citation between Timothy's entry and the Elders tier by narrowing Timothy's 5:21-23 citation down to 5:23 alone (his own personal health instruction), leaving 5:21-22 solely and fully covered by the Elders That Rule Well tier where that procedural charge actually belongs.

scribeTiers.scribeName: Doctrines of Devils in the Latter Times

characters.name: Paul the Apostle

verses.note: Paul, an apostle by the commandment of God, writes to Timothy, 'my own son in the faith,' with grace, mercy, and peace.
Recounts besought Timothy to abide still at Ephesus, to charge some that they teach no other doctrine — the occasion for the letter.

Paul's personal testimony: was formerly a blasphemer, persecutor, and injurious, yet obtained mercy because he did it ignorantly in unbelief; Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom Paul says he is chief; held up as a pattern to them that should believe.
Doxology immediately following his testimony: 'Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.'
Commits this charge to Timothy according to the prophecies which went before on him; names Hymenaeus and Alexander as those he has delivered unto Satan that they may learn not to blaspheme.
Exhorts that prayer be made for all men; states he was ordained a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
Writes these things hoping to come to Timothy shortly, but in case he tarries, so Timothy may know how to behave himself in the house of God.
Instructs Timothy to put the brethren in remembrance of these things, to command and teach them, and to give attendance to reading, exhortation, and doctrine till Paul comes.
Final closing charge to keep that which is committed to his trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings and oppositions of science falsely so called.

funFacts: Paul's self-description as formerly 'a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious' (1:13) echoes his history as a persecutor of the church described in Acts 9, though Acts itself is a separate book.
Calls himself 'chief' of sinners (1:15) — one of the strongest self-descriptions Paul gives of his own past anywhere in his letters.

characters.name: Timothy

genealogy.father: unnamed Greek father — Acts 16:1, not itself part of this book's text
genealogy.mother: eunice — 2 Timothy 1:5, described there as 'a Jewess, and believed,' not individually indexed in this book

verses.note: Addressed by Paul as 'my own son in the faith.'
Besought by Paul to abide still at Ephesus, to charge certain men that they teach no other doctrine.
This charge is committed to Timothy according to the prophecies which went before on him, that he might war a good warfare.
Told to let no man despise his youth, but to be an example of the believers in word, conversation, charity, spirit, faith, purity.

Told to give attendance to reading, exhortation, and doctrine; not to neglect the gift given him by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery; to meditate on these things and take heed to himself and his doctrine, to continue in them for the sake of himself and his hearers.
Instructed how to treat elder men, younger men, elder women, and younger women within the church — as fathers, brothers, mothers, sisters, with all purity.
Told to drink no longer water only, but to use a little wine for his stomach's sake and his often infirmities.

Called 'O man of God' and charged to flee covetous things, follow righteousness, and fight the good fight of faith, keeping the commandment without spot until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ; the charge closes with a doxology describing God as 'the blessed and only Potentate, King of kings, and Lord of lords... to whom be honour and power everlasting.'
Final address: 'O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust.'

funFacts: Acts 16:1-3 records Timothy's mother as 'a Jewess, and believed' and his father as 'a Greek' — background not stated within 1 Timothy itself but relevant to the personal relationship the letter is built on.
1 Timothy 4:14 references 'the gift that is in thee...given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery,' generally understood as referring to Timothy's own ordination.

characters.name: Hymenaeus and Alexander
characters.perkNote: The text groups these two together without differentiating their individual actions (1:19-20), so they are indexed as one collective entry rather than split. A Hymenaeus also reappears paired with Philetus in 2 Timothy 2:17, and an Alexander the coppersmith appears separately in 2 Timothy 4:14 — the text never explicitly identifies either as the same man named here, so no identity across the letters is asserted.

verses.note: Named as examples of those who, having put away a good conscience, made shipwreck concerning the faith; Paul says he has delivered them unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.

characters.name: Fables and Endless Genealogies
characters.purpose: Warns against speculative teaching — myths, genealogical disputes, and misapplied use of the Mosaic law — that ministers questions rather than godly edifying, and bookends the letter with the same caution against quarrelsome false doctrine.

verses.note: Charge that some teach no other doctrine, nor give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions rather than godly edifying.
The end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart; some have turned aside to vain jangling, desiring to be teachers of the law, understanding neither what they say nor whereof they affirm.
The law is good if a man use it lawfully, knowing it is made not for a righteous man but for the lawless and disobedient, according to the glorious gospel committed to Paul's trust.
Closing echo of the same warning: avoid profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called, which some professing have erred concerning the faith.

characters.name: Prayers, Supplications, and Intercessions
characters.purpose: Instructs the church to pray broadly, including for kings and civil authority, grounding the instruction in God's universal will to save and Christ's role as the one mediator between God and men.

verses.note: Exhorts that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men, for kings and all in authority, that believers may lead a quiet and peaceable life.
This is good and acceptable in God's sight, who will have all men to be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth.
There is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom for all.
Paul states he was ordained a preacher, apostle, and teacher of the Gentiles; men everywhere are to pray, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting.

characters.name: The Woman's Adornment and Silence
characters.purpose: Sets instructions for women's dress and conduct in the gathered church, grounding the teaching in the Genesis creation and fall order — Adam formed first, then Eve, and Eve deceived.

verses.note: Women to adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety, not with broided hair, gold, pearls, or costly array, but with good works.
Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection; not permitted to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.
For Adam was first formed, then Eve; Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.
She shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety.

characters.name: The Bishop's Qualifications
characters.purpose: Lists the moral character and household qualifications required of anyone who desires to oversee a local church.

verses.note: If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.

A bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre, but patient, not a brawler, not covetous.
One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; for if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?
Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil; must have a good report of those outside the church.

characters.name: The Deacon's Qualifications
characters.purpose: Sets equivalent moral qualifications for deacons and their wives, the second recognized office of the church alongside the bishop/overseer.

verses.note: Deacons must be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre, holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
Let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.
Their wives must likewise be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.
Deacons to be husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well; those who have used the office well purchase to themselves a good degree and great boldness in the faith.

characters.name: The Mystery of Godliness
characters.purpose: A short creedal, hymn-like doctrinal statement summarizing the incarnation and proclamation of Christ, given as the theological center that the church — 'the pillar and ground of the truth' — exists to uphold.

verses.note: Paul writes hoping to come to Timothy shortly, but in case he tarries long, so Timothy may know how to behave himself in the house of God, the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

Without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.

characters.name: Doctrines of Devils in the Latter Times
characters.scribeTier: Doctrines of Devils in the Latter Times
characters.purpose: Warns of a coming falling-away marked by false asceticism — forbidding marriage, forbidding foods — countered first by the teaching that everything God created is good and rightly received with thanksgiving, then by a direct positive charge to refuse profane and old wives' fables and instead exercise unto godliness, since godliness (unlike mere bodily discipline) profits both the life that now is and the life to come.

verses.note: The Spirit speaketh expressly that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of devils, speaking lies in hypocrisy, having their conscience seared with a hot iron.
Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.
Every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving, for it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.

Charged to refuse profane and old wives' fables, and to exercise himself rather unto godliness; for bodily exercise profiteth little, but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come; this is a faithful saying, for Paul and his companions labour and suffer reproach because they trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.

characters.name: The Widow Indeed
characters.purpose: Sets criteria for the church's care of widows and for enrolling certain widows into a recognized order of service, distinguishing genuine need (a 'widow indeed') from cases a widow's own family or remarriage should properly address.

verses.note: Honour widows that are widows indeed.
If a widow have children or nephews, let them first learn to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents.
She that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day; but she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth.
These things give in charge, that they may be blameless — Timothy is told to command the preceding instructions about honoring true widows and family responsibility.
If any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.

A widow taken into the number should not be under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man, well reported of for good works — bringing up children, lodging strangers, washing the saints' feet, relieving the afflicted, diligently following every good work.

The younger widows to be refused; when they wax wanton against Christ they will marry, having damnation because they have cast off their first faith, and learn to be idle, wandering about as tattlers and busybodies.
Paul's counsel that the younger widows marry, bear children, guide the house, and give no occasion to the adversary, since some have already turned aside after Satan.
If any believing man or woman have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged, that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.

characters.name: Elders That Rule Well
characters.purpose: Sets protocol for honoring, correcting, and ordaining elders, guarding the process against favoritism and hasty judgment.

verses.note: Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine.
For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn, and, The labourer is worthy of his reward.
Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.
Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear.
Charges Timothy before God, the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, to observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality.
Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins; keep thyself pure.
Some men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment, and some men they follow after; likewise the good works of some are manifest beforehand, and those that are otherwise cannot be hid.

characters.name: Servants Under the Yoke
characters.purpose: Instructs Christian bondservants on honoring their masters, framed around protecting the church's reputation and rightly valuing a believing master as a brother rather than presuming on the relationship.

verses.note: As many servants as are under the yoke are to count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.
Those with believing masters are not to despise them because they are brethren, but rather do them service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit.

characters.name: The Love of Money
characters.purpose: Warns against false teachers who treat godliness as a means of profit, and instructs both the discontented — that godliness with contentment is itself great gain — and the already-rich, to be generous rather than trust in uncertain riches.

verses.note: If any teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words and doctrine according to godliness, he is proud, knowing nothing, doting about questions and strifes of words, from which come envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings, and perverse disputings of corrupt minds supposing that gain is godliness.
Godliness with contentment is great gain; we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out; having food and raiment, let us be content.

They that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare; the love of money is the root of all evil, which some coveting after have erred from the faith and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
Charge them that are rich in this world that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy.
That they do good, be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate; laying up in store a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

pontius_pilate_reference.note: Christ Jesus is described as having 'before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession' — cited only as a historical reference point for Christ's own testimony (part of Timothy's 6:11-16 charge), not as an active character within this book, so no separate character entry is made for Pilate here.

timothy_family_background.note: Timothy's father (unnamed Greek), mother (Eunice), and grandmother (Lois) are described elsewhere in scripture but not within 1 Timothy itself; noted here for completeness rather than indexed as separate characters in this book.
